title: Securities Trading Policy (Schedule 9)

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors and officers of the Group including the Managing Director; all persons who report directly to the CEO (Senior Executives); all employees, consultants and contractors of the Group; and other persons identified by the Company from time to time. All additional restrictions (closed periods, clearance, hedging ban-with-consent, short-term trading discouragement) apply to this tier without differentiation, other than the identity of the Authorising Officer.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The chair of the Board; distinguished only for the Authorising Officer table (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) and mandatory prior notification to the Company Secretary and Board.

tiers.name: Other Directors (including Managing Director)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, including the Managing Director; distinguished only for the Authorising Officer table (Chair of the Board) and mandatory prior notification to the Company Secretary and Board.

tiers.name: Senior Executives, and other persons identified by the Company from time to time
tiers.description: Persons reporting directly to the CEO, and other persons the Company identifies; distinguished only for the Authorising Officer table (Managing Director) and mandatory prior notification to the Company Secretary and Board.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees generally; distinguished only for the Authorising Officer table (Managing Director) and mandatory prior notification to the Company Secretary and Board.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse or partner; children; relatives (or spouse/partner's relatives) sharing the same home address; trustees of a trust under which the person, spouse/partner or dependent children is a beneficiary; companies where the person is a director, senior officer or controlling/majority shareholder; non-limited partners of a partnership the person is in; entities where the person is a director, secretary or executive officer; and BCBCA-defined affiliates of any of the foregoing.

definitions.hedging_definition: engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities

windows.end_anchor: conclusion of the business day on which the Company's quarterly results are released to the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The board of directors may decide 'any other period' as an additional Closed Period (clause 20.2); the policy does not state whether such additional periods are confidential, though a refusal of trading approval generally 'must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone' (clause 23).

rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives (expressly including put and call options) related to Company Securities requires prior written approval by the Authorising Officer; the requirement is expressly extended to Securities that are unvested, holding-locked or issued under an equity-based remuneration scheme (no outright ban at any vesting state).
rules.evidence: must not, without prior written approval by the Authorising Officer specified in clauses 21 to 24, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements or any arrangement limiting economic risk in connection with Company Securities require prior written approval, expressly including unvested, holding-locked or equity-remuneration-scheme securities; not an outright ban at any vesting state.
rules.evidence: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a structure that secures a profit or avoids a loss from price fluctuations (e.g. a prepaid forward) falls within the broad catch-all and requires the same prior written approval.
rules.evidence: other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. As a trade in Company Securities it requires prior written clearance and two trading days' notice under the general dealing procedure, and may separately be caught as an arrangement to secure a profit from price fluctuations under clause 27.
rules.evidence: If a Restricted Person proposes to deal in the Company's Securities at any time, they must first obtain prior written clearance to deal in the Company's Securities from the relevant authorising officer

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are expressly named as requiring the same prior written approval as hedging/derivatives, with no outright ban at any vesting state.
rules.evidence: dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is not separately banned. The exemption for a lender's forced sale presupposes that the underlying margin lending arrangement was itself set up with prior approval 'in accordance with this policy', implying the ordinary clearance procedure applies to entering it.
rules.evidence: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy

rules.detail: Granting security over Company Securities is not separately named, but is implicit in the 'secured financing arrangement' referred to as needing prior approval before a lender's later forced sale is exempt.
rules.evidence: a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement in respect of Company Securities (not limited to margin loans) is implicitly subject to prior approval under the general clearance procedure; no outright ban stated at any vesting state.
rules.evidence: a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy

rules.detail: No defined holding period; the policy discourages (in aspirational 'should not' terms, rather than 'must not') short-term or speculative trading.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company's Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging permitted with consent even when unvested
bespoke_clauses.clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban hedging of unvested securities outright, BMC's policy only requires prior written approval regardless of vesting state, so a collar over unvested or holding-locked plan securities is not automatically barred, only gated by approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once the loan securing the collar has been approved, the bank's later enforcement sale is a pre-approved 'permitted dealing' available at any time, including in a Closed Period, removing forced-sale timing risk for the lender.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within 5 trading days and before any inside information arises, or the clearance evaporates automatically without notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The insider trading prohibitions apply even when a trade falls within an exclusion to the restrictions on trading detailed in this policy if it is undertaken by, or procured by, someone in possession of inside information at the time of the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the margin-lender forced-sale exemption could be challenged if the disposal is 'procured by' an executive who holds inside information at the time, so enforcement timing during blackout-adjacent periods carries residual risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the affiliates (as such term is used in the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) ...) of any of the foregoing
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an affiliated entity or controlled company does not escape the approval requirement, as BCBCA-style affiliates are Associates under the policy.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, subject to prior written approval rather than an outright ban. Clause 27 requires Restricted Persons to obtain prior written approval from the relevant Authorising Officer before dealing in derivatives, hedging arrangements or other arrangements varying economic risk (expressly including put and call options and CFDs), and this requirement extends even to unvested, holding-locked or equity-scheme securities, so there is no vesting-based prohibition. Secured financing and margin lending are not separately banned; clause 29.5 exempts a lender's forced sale once the underlying secured financing arrangement has itself been approved 'in accordance with this policy', implying the loan leg also needs prior clearance but can then proceed, including lender enforcement during a Closed Period. Clearance is valid for only five trading days and is automatically withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information before trading, so the collar and loan must be documented and executed promptly after approval. Directors and Senior Executives must route approval through the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, or the Managing Director as applicable, and any forced sale procured while the executive holds inside information remains a breach notwithstanding the exemption.
